#en:
I used to stock shelves in a corner shop on Cydonia. Eight hours of lining up canned beans and nutrient bricks, straightening labels that nobody ever read. Coworkers whose names I barely remember now, faces blurred together under bad strip lights. I told myself it was temporary, just a way to stay fed until enlistment. Funny how that kind of work trains you to stop thinking about what you are touching, just move it from one place to another and trust it belongs there.  

The service felt like more of the same at first. Marcus Havel tossed me the boring details: inventorying ammo pallets, checking seals on med crates, escort duty on transports that never should have seen contact. "Prove you can count and shut up," he said. Only later did I find out some of those crates never existed on any manifest, that we were moving things no one wanted traced back to a flag. Elias Korrin made a joke once about how the safest missions were always the ones no one was allowed to talk about afterward. We laughed, because the alternative was asking why.  

Obsidian did not happen overnight. It was a long series of "temporary" compromises. The op in that burned-out colony where we were told to escort civilians to safety, then quietly reassign the gunship overwatch before the pirates came back. The patrol routes that always seemed to leave one corridor conveniently unwatched, the same corridor certain freighters had been nudged into following. I remember sitting in a debrief, hearing words like "deniable" and "acceptable drift," and realizing they were describing people, not numbers.  

I think about that sometimes when I herd my own squad through another contract. Different patch, same formation. We still clear corners like we did in uniform, still call out targets with proper brevity, still police our brass if we have the time. Marcus pretends he does not miss the old structure, but he still checks our kit like an old sergeant on inspection. Elias runs the comms like a proper officer, even if the only command now is whoever is wiring credits to a dummy account. Discipline did not die when we walked; it just serves a smaller circle.  

There was a moment, not long ago, when I flinched at my own reflection. We were in a decommissioned listening post, cleaning up after someone else's mess, and I caught my face in a cracked console screen. Visor up, eyes flat, giving orders I used to associate with the men I hated: "No witnesses," "Leave the bodies where they fall," "We were never here." I could hear my own tone, controlled and cold, and I recognized it from back when I was the one receiving those lines over the radio and clenching my jaw. Somewhere along the chain, I became the voice.  

I still remember that shop back on Cydonia. The rhythm of stacking, sweeping, clocking out. A job that was never meant to lead anywhere, one I told myself I was too good for. Now my days are just a different kind of stocking, moving people and weapons through corridors someone else has drawn, trusting they "belong" where we put them. The pay is better, the tasks are sharper, and every time I tell a recruit that the first job is just to count and shut up, I hear the echo of an officer I once feared and realize I have grown into his shadow.
zh:
我以前在赛多尼亚一家街角小店摆货架。八小时把罐装豆子和营养砖码好，把没人会读的标签摆正。同事的名字我如今几乎记不住，脸在劣质条形灯下糊成一片。我告诉自己那是暂时的，只是入伍前混口饭吃。有趣的是，那种活儿训练你不再去想自己在碰什么，只把它从一个地方挪到另一个地方，并相信它本该在那儿。

服役起初感觉也差不多。马库斯·哈维尔把那些无聊的细节丢给我：清点弹药货板、检查医疗箱封条、护送那些本不该遭遇交战的运输。他说"证明你会数数然后闭嘴"。只是后来我才发现，其中一些箱子在任何清单上都不存在，我们在运没人希望被追溯回某面旗帜的东西。伊莱亚斯·科林曾开玩笑说，最安全的任务永远是不许人在事后谈论的那些。我们都笑了，因为另一条路是问为什么。

黑曜石不是一夜之间出现的。它是一连串"临时"的妥协。那次在烧毁的殖民地，我们被告知把平民护送到安全处，然后在海盗回来之前悄悄把炮艇的瞭望调走。那些巡逻路线似乎总留下一条走廊方便地无人看守，而某些货船正是被引向那条走廊。我记得坐在一次述职里，听到"可否认"和"可接受漂移"这类词，意识到他们描述的是人，不是数字。

有时我带着自己的小队跑另一份合同时会想起这个。不同的臂章，同样的编队。我们仍像穿制服时那样清角、仍用规范的简短术语报目标、有时间就仍把弹壳收拾干净。马库斯假装他不怀念旧秩序，可他仍像老军士长视察一样检查我们的装备。伊莱亚斯像正规军官一样管通讯，哪怕如今的"指挥"只是谁在往一个假账户打钱。我们离开时纪律没有死；它只是服务于一个更小的圈子。

不久前有那么一刻，我对自己在倒影里的样子畏缩了。我们在一座退役的监听站里清理别人留下的烂摊子，我在一块裂开的控制台屏幕里瞥见自己的脸。面罩抬起，眼神平淡，下达着我曾与那些我恨的人联系在一起的命令："不留目击者""尸体就留在倒下的地方""我们从没来过这儿"。我能听见自己的语调，克制而冰冷，而我认得出它——从前我是那个在无线电里接收这些话、咬紧牙关的人。在链条的某处，我成了那个声音。

我仍记得赛多尼亚那家小店。摆货、扫地、打卡下班的节奏。一份从不打算通向任何地方的活儿，一份我告诉自己我配不上干的活儿。如今我的日子只是另一种摆货，把人和武器沿着别人画好的走廊挪动，相信他们"本该"在我们放下的地方。报酬更好，任务更锋利，而每次我告诉新人第一份活儿就是数数然后闭嘴时，我都听见一个我曾畏惧的军官的回声，意识到自己长成了他的影子。

#en:
Mutineer Platoon Safehouse  
Shipboard Quiet Cycle  

Rowan says we are free now. Says walking out on the chain of command means we finally get to choose the terms of our own fights. I keep waiting for the feeling to land. Instead, every time I lace my boots, my hands move like there is still a schedule somewhere with my name slotted into a firing line and a colonel ready to mark me late. Discipline sticks deeper than shrapnel. We still clean weapons on rotation, still check each other's gear, still sleep with boots within arm's reach. Only difference is, if someone gives a bad order now, we do not pretend we did not hear it. We look at each other, then at the one who spoke, and the silence decides whether that person walks out of the room.

Saw Alina running sims again, cycling through that same orbital insertion scenario command used for the "training exercise" over the colony that was not supposed to exist. I remember the after-action, the way the briefers danced around the civilian transponders that lit up our boards at the last second, called them "sensor ghosts" and "legacy beacons." We all knew better. They scrubbed the records hard, but not hard enough. Rumor has it someone in a breaker crew pulled the real logs out of a wreck and started asking for prices. That is when the missions got stranger. Targets that looked like pirates on paper but moved like professionals, "salvage disputes" that mysteriously aligned with disputed reports from the war. They kept telling us it was about stability. It sounded a lot like self-preservation.

I still think about the moment I started lying as easily as breathing. It was back when I rode the shuttle from the barracks to the training grounds every morning, same seat, same scratched window, same view of the shipyard cranes ticking across the skyline. I would lean my head against the glass and rehearse answers for inspections, for ops review, for the questions I knew my partner would throw at me when I finally got a break. Where were you, why did you not call, why does your gear smell like burning metal. The first time I told him everything was fine, that we were just running extended drills and nothing was out of the ordinary, it slid out smoother than the truth. I watched the reflection of my mouth in that shuttle window and realized I meant it more than I should have. Every apology he ever gave me came dressed in explanations, reasons why he could not change, why this time would be different if only I understood. It took me longer than I like to admit to realize that was not an apology, just preemptive absolution. When command started talking the same way, I knew exactly what it was.

Darren still thinks we can fix something from out here, that if we pull the right thread we can drag the truth into daylight without burning everything else down. Kara does not talk about fixing anything; she just makes sure our kits are stocked and our exit vectors are clean. I sit somewhere between them, nursing the old habits and the new loyalties, wondering how many more "ghost beacons" and "salvage disputes" we would have marched through if we had stayed. Walking away from the flag was easy in the moment. Living with where we walked to is the part nobody wrote a manual for.
zh:
哗变排安全屋
船上静默周期

罗文说我们现在自由了。说走出指挥链意味着我们终于能选择自己战斗的条款。我一直在等那种感觉落地。可每一次我系靴带，我的手都按着像还有个日程表、上面把我排进某条射击线、还有个上校准备记我迟到。纪律扎得比弹片还深。我们仍轮流擦武器、仍检查彼此的装备、仍把靴子放在一臂之内睡觉。唯一的区别是，如今要是有人下坏命令，我们不假装没听见。我们看着彼此，再看说话的那个人，而沉默决定那个人能否走出这个房间。

看见阿丽娜又跑模拟了，一遍遍循环指挥部用在那个本不该存在的殖民地上方"训练演习"的同一套入轨情景。我记得那次行动后，简报人如何绕着最后一秒在我们主板上亮起的民用应答器打转，管它们叫"传感器幽灵"和"遗留信标"。我们心里都清楚。他们把记录擦得很狠，但不够狠。传言说某支拆解队的人从一具残骸里扒出了真实日志，然后开始问价。就是从那时起，任务变得更古怪。纸面上像海盗、动起来却像专业人员的那些目标，与战争中争议报告神秘吻合的"打捞纠纷"。他们一直告诉我们这是为了稳定。听起来很像自保。

我仍想起我开始把撒谎说得像呼吸一样容易的那一刻。那时我每天早上从营房坐班车去训练场，同一个座位、同一扇刮花的窗、同样看着船坞吊车在天际线上咔哒扫过。我会把头靠在玻璃上，为检查、为行动复盘、为我知道搭档终于在我休息时会抛给我的问题排练答案。你在哪儿、你为什么不打电话、你的装备为什么闻起来像烧焦的金属。我第一次告诉他一切都好、我们只是在跑延长训练、没什么异常时，它滑出来比真相还顺。我看着那扇班车窗户里自己嘴的倒影，意识到我比该有的更信它。他给过我的每一句道歉都披着解释的外衣，理由是他不能改、只要我理解这次就会不一样。我花了比我想承认的更久才明白，那不是道歉，只是预防性的赦免。当指挥部开始用同样的方式说话时，我立刻明白那是什么。

达伦仍觉得我们能从这里修好什么，说只要拉对线头，就能把真相拖到光下而不把别的都烧掉。卡拉不谈修好任何东西；她只确保我们的装备备足、撤离矢量干净。我坐在他们之间某处，照料着旧习惯和新忠诚，琢磨要是我们留下来，还会列队穿过多少"幽灵信标"和"打捞纠纷"。当下离开那面旗帜很容易。带着我们走到的地方活下去，才是没人写过手册的部分。

#en:
I woke up reaching for my rifle again. No alarm, no boarding klaxon, just muscle memory and the echo of that old shipboard tone in my head. Malik Arden laughed when he saw me halfway out of the bunk, boots on the wrong feet, but his eyes did that distant thing. We all do it. The Lancers pretend we are done taking orders, but our bodies have not received the memo.

Sofia Trent spent the morning checking firing arcs like we still had a command inspection coming. Her hands moved on their own, measuring clearances, calling out blind spots to nobody. Darius Kellan told her to relax, that nobody above deck twelve cares how straight our lines are anymore, but he still double-checked every magazine himself. We may have walked away from the uniform, but the uniform did not walk out of us.

Naomi Vance brought up that op again, the one with the "noncombatants" we were ordered not to see. Officially they were not there. Unofficially I can still hear the screaming over the comms when the building came down. They said the intel was clean, that the blame sat with a miscalibrated sensor. Funny how miscalibration looks just like someone deciding not to look too closely. We were good soldiers back then. We shut up, signed the nondisclosures, and told ourselves the medal made it worth it.

Sometimes I think that is where the Redacted Lancers really started, in that debrief room with the air scrubbers humming too loud and the brass refusing to meet our eyes. Alexis Rowe kept clenching and unclenching her fists under the table, knuckles white. Afterward she punched a bulkhead so hard she cracked a knuckle, then smiled through the blood like it was the first honest thing she had felt in months. Now she is the one keeping our trigger discipline sharp, like a worshipper tending a broken shrine.

There was a moment planetside last month I cannot shake. Ambush in the alleys, comms jammed, someone up the chain "forgetting" to mention the second hostile cell. We ended up back-to-back behind a crumbling wall, me and Sofia pressed so tight we could barely breathe, hands locked together to keep from being separated when the shockwave hit. It was not affection, not even trust; it was survival instinct, two ghosts refusing to drift apart before the next shell landed. Later we let go and went back to pretending touch means nothing in this outfit.

Every now and then I ask myself why I stayed when the others burned their IDs and ran for civilian names. The answer is always ugly. Leaving felt more terrifying than enduring the pain I already knew. Out there I am just another discharged number at the mercy of whatever lie the next employer is selling. In here, at least, I recognize the lies, and the people telling them wear the same scars I do.

We say we are done with command, but Redacted Lancers is still a kind of order, just written in blood and regret instead of ink. We look out for each other because nobody else will, and because if we stop, we will have to admit we became exactly what we swore we were never fighting for. Tonight I will clean my rifle, listen to Malik and Darius argue over tactics like the old days, and try not to think about the names on the classified casualty lists that never made it home. It is easier that way.
zh:
我又一次在醒来时伸手去摸步枪。没有警报、没有登船钟，只有肌肉记忆和我脑子里那声旧船载提示音的回响。马利克·阿登看见我半爬出铺位、靴子穿反了时笑了，可他的眼睛做了那种出神的事。我们都这样。枪骑兵们假装我们不再接受命令，可我们的身体没收到那份备忘录。

索菲亚·特伦特花了一早上检查射击弧，像我们还有一次指挥检查要来。她的手自己动着，测量间隙，向无人报出盲点。大流士·凯兰叫她放松，说十二层甲板以上的人再也不在乎我们的线直不直了，可他自己还是把每个弹匣都复查一遍。我们也许离开了制服，但制服没有离开我们。

娜奥米·万斯又提起那次行动，那批"被命令不许看见"的"非战斗人员"。官方上他们不在那儿。非官方地，我仍能听见楼塌时通讯里的尖叫。他们说情报是干净的，责任在一台校准失准的传感器。有趣的是，"失准"看起来就像有人决定不细看。那时我们是好兵。我们闭嘴、签下保密协议，告诉自己那枚奖章让一切值得。

有时我想，被涂黑的枪骑兵就是在那间述职室里真正开始的——空气净化器嗡鸣得太响，长官们拒绝与我们对视。亚历克西斯·罗在桌下不断攥紧又松开拳头，指节发白。事后她一拳砸在舱壁上，砸裂了一个指节，然后带着血笑，像那是她几个月来感到的第一件诚实的事。如今正是她在让我们的扳机纪律保持锋利，像信徒照料一座破败的神龛。

上个月行星表面有个瞬间我甩不掉。小巷里遭伏击，通讯被干扰，指挥链上有人"忘了"提第二处敌巢。我们最后背靠背躲在一堵塌墙上，我和索菲亚贴得几乎不能呼吸，双手扣在一起，好让冲击波来时不被分开。那不是感情，甚至不是信任；是求生本能，两个鬼在下一发炮弹落地前拒绝散开。后来我们松开手，回去假装在这支部队里触碰什么都不算。

时不时我会问自己，别人烧掉身份跑去当平民时，我为什么留下。答案总是丑陋的。离开比忍受我已熟悉的痛苦更可怕。在外面，我只是又一个退役编号，任由下一个雇主兜售的谎言摆布。在这里，至少我认得出谎言，而说谎言的人带着和我一样的伤疤。

我们说我们不再受指挥，可涂黑枪骑兵仍是一种秩序，只是用血和悔恨而不是墨水写成。我们互相照应，因为没有别人会，也因为要是我们停下来，就得承认自己变成了我们发誓从不为它战斗的那种东西。今晚我会擦我的步枪，听马利克和大流士像旧日那样为战术争论，尽量不去想那些从没回家的密级伤亡名单上的名字。那样更容易。

#en:
Did a dry run with Unit today. Maya on point, Elena on rear security, me in the middle pretending not to watch both of them too closely. On paper it was just another corridor-clearing sim, but Command loaded the targets with civvy silhouettes at the last minute and never said why. Elena did not even twitch. Maya hesitated once, half a heartbeat, then corrected. Afterward nobody mentioned it. That is the first rule around here: whatever gets under your skin, you seal it in with the rest of the scars and call it "experience."

Between rotations I found myself straightening the weapons racks in the team bay, checking latches, wiping down plates that were already clean. Hand remembered the rhythm before my head did. Same movements from when I used to help my uncle close his repair shop back home, sweeping floors and tightening bolts on haulers for people I would never see again. Back then, I just did the chores because that is what you do for family. Somewhere along the line it stopped being about helping and started being about not feeling anything while I worked. Turns out that trick is hard to turn off; numbing out kept me sane in the field, but now I catch myself doing it over a cup of coffee, over a casualty report, over Maya's quiet shake in the hands when she thinks nobody is looking.

There is more noise on the net about "weather work" contracts lately. Cargo outfits wanting escort through systems that should be calm, colonies talking about freak storms like someone flipped a switch. One of the handlers dropped a name in the mess, then swallowed it with his drink like he regretted letting it out. Word is there is a specialist out there who can move fog and rain the way we move fireteams, and every major player either wants her on a leash or in a body bag. Elena thinks it is just another ghost story to justify hazard pay. Maya listens and says nothing, but I have seen the way her eyes track the forecast graphs on the mission boards.

Unit pretends to be apolitical, just a clean logo stamped on dirty jobs. Truth is, loyalties shift with the contracts. Half the squad owes favors to one corp or another, and the other half thinks nobody has noticed. We never talk about it out loud, but it shows in where people stand on the range, who drills together, who always volunteers for "optional" insertions. I have gotten good at not caring who signs the cred transfers, only that the op is clear and the extraction is on time. That is another kind of numbness, I guess. Hard to remember what it felt like to believe in something beyond the next deployment and the state of my rifle.

Tonight the air recyclers have that cold-metal taste that says someone has been running simulations in the background for hours. There will be a briefing soon, another job dressed up as stabilization or protection or "mitigating emergent anomalies." Maybe it is tied to these storm rumors, maybe it is just more station clearance and quiet denials. Either way, I will suit up when they call. I will check Maya's harness, trade a nod with Elena, and push everything else down where it cannot get in the way. I tell myself I will stop living like that one day, that I will let myself feel the weight of what we do. But not tomorrow. Tomorrow, there is work.
zh:
今天和部队做了次演练。玛雅打头，埃琳娜殿后警戒，我在中间假装没太仔细地同时盯着她们俩。纸面上那只是又一次清走廊模拟，可指挥部在最后一刻给靶子加载了平民剪影，还没说为什么。埃琳娜连眉都没动。玛雅犹豫了一次，半拍心跳，然后修正了。事后没人提起。这是这儿的第一条规矩：任何钻进你皮肤底下的东西，你都把它和其余伤疤一起封进去，管它叫"经验"。

轮班之间，我发觉自己在队部里整理武器架，检查卡扣，擦拭本就干净的枪身。手比脑子先记起那节奏。同样的动作，来自我以前帮叔叔收铺子的时候——在家里扫地、给再也见不到的客人拧紧货船的螺栓。那时我做家务只是因为那是为家人做的事。一路上某处，它不再是为了帮忙，而成了干活时不去感觉任何东西。原来那种把戏很难关掉；麻木让我在战场上保持清醒，可如今我发觉自己在一杯咖啡上、在一份伤亡报告上、在玛雅以为没人看时手轻轻发抖时，也这么做。

网上近来关于"天气作业"合同的噪声更多了。货运公司在要求护送穿过本该平静的星系，殖民地在谈论像有人拨动了开关的诡异风暴。一个办事员在食堂里抖出一个名字，然后又就着酒咽了回去，像后悔让它溜出来。传闻说外面有个专家能像我们移动火力小组那样移动雾和雨，而每个大玩家要么想把她拴上绳，要么想把她装进尸袋。埃琳娜觉得那只是又一个为危险津贴找理由的鬼故事。玛雅听着，什么都不说，可我见过她的眼睛如何追踪任务板上的预报图。

部队假装不问政治，只是盖在脏活儿上的一个干净标志。事实是，忠诚随合同漂移。一半小队欠这家或那家企业的人情，另一半以为没人注意到。我们从不公开谈这个，但它体现在人们在靶场的站位、谁一起操练、谁总是自愿去"可选"插入。我已经擅长不去在乎谁签那些信用转账，只在乎行动清晰、撤离准时。那，我猜，是另一种麻木。很难记起相信超越下一次部署和步枪状态的东西是什么感觉。

今晚空气回收机带着那种冷金属味，说明有人在后台跑了几个小时的模拟。很快会有一份简报，另一份包装成稳定、保护或"缓解新现异常"的活儿。也许它跟这些风暴传言有关，也许只是更多的站点清理和安静否认。无论哪种，他们一叫我就穿装备。我会检查玛雅的背带，和埃琳娜交换一个点头，把其余一切都压到它碍不着事的地方。我告诉自己有一天我会停止这样活，会让自己感受我们所做之事的重量。但不是明天。明天有活儿。
